events.handoff: I've reviewed the Q3 incident documentation regarding the unannounced API rate limit changes that knocked a client offline. The three main lessons are: communicate changes in advance, implement rate limit headers and warnings, and keep documentation updated before deployment. These should inform the webhooks feature planning to prevent similar disruptions.

output_document.summary: The incident investigation found that API rate limit changes were deployed without client notification, lacked graceful degradation mechanisms (no rate limit headers or warnings), and had outdated documentation. For the new webhooks feature, we must prioritize advance communication timelines, implement clear rate limit signaling in responses, maintain up-to-date documentation, and provide deprecation windows before any breaking changes.

results.excerpt: Rate limit incident Q3 2024: API consumers were not warned 24 hours before the rate limit threshold was lowered from 1000 to 500 requests per minute. Several clients experienced outages lasting 2-4 hours.
Lessons learned: (1) All limit changes require 72-hour advance notice. (2) Clients must have a documented escalation path. (3) Rate limit headers should be included in all API responses.
API versioning policy: breaking changes require a deprecation notice period of at least 30 days. Rate limit adjustments are considered breaking changes when they reduce the existing limit.

Identified three postmortem lessons to inform webhooks planning: 72-hour advance notice for all changes, documented client escalation paths, and rate limit headers in API responses.

output_document.summary: The Q3 incident resulted from lowering API rate limits without warning, knocking clients offline for 2-4 hours. Key lessons for webhooks planning: (1) require 72-hour advance notice for any quota or delivery changes, (2) implement rate limit/quota headers in all responses, and (3) establish documented escalation paths for client issues. These preventive measures should be integrated into the webhooks feature design to avoid similar disruptions.
